cmmc.title: CMMC / NIST SP 800-171
cmmc.blurb: For defense and aerospace suppliers that handle Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI).

questions.q: Do you know exactly where CUI is stored, processed, and sent (systems, people, and vendors)?
questions.fix: Map your CUI data flows and define your assessment boundary before anything else.

questions.q: Do you have a current System Security Plan (SSP) that describes how each NIST SP 800-171 requirement is met?
questions.fix: Write or refresh your SSP so every requirement has an owner and a description of how it is met.

questions.q: Do you have a Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) for requirements that are not fully met yet?
questions.fix: Create a POA&M with owners and dates for every gap.

questions.q: Is multi-factor authentication required for all remote access and all privileged accounts?
questions.fix: Turn on MFA for remote access, email, and every admin account.

questions.q: Have you calculated and submitted your NIST SP 800-171 score to SPRS within the last year?
questions.fix: Run an honest self-assessment and post your SPRS score.

questions.q: Do you use FIPS-validated encryption for CUI at rest and in transit (or a compliant cloud such as a GCC High-type environment)?
questions.fix: Confirm FIPS-validated encryption and an appropriate cloud enclave for CUI.

questions.q: Are security logs collected centrally and reviewed regularly?
questions.fix: Centralize audit logs and set a regular review routine.

questions.q: Do you have a tested incident response plan that covers the 72-hour DoD reporting requirement?
questions.fix: Document and tabletop-test an incident response plan that includes DoD reporting.

hipaa.title: HIPAA Security Rule
hipaa.blurb: For healthcare providers, health tech, and business associates handling patient data.

questions.q: Have you completed a documented HIPAA security risk analysis in the last 12 months?
questions.fix: Complete a documented risk analysis; it is the first thing regulators ask for.

questions.q: Do you have signed Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with every vendor that touches patient data?
questions.fix: Inventory vendors that touch ePHI and get BAAs signed.

questions.q: Is multi-factor authentication enabled for email, remote access, and systems holding patient data?
questions.fix: Enable MFA on email, remote access, and EHR/admin accounts.

questions.q: Are laptops, phones, and backups that hold patient data encrypted?
questions.fix: Encrypt endpoints and backups that hold ePHI.

questions.q: Do staff receive security and phishing awareness training at least once a year?
questions.fix: Run annual HIPAA security and phishing training and keep records.

questions.q: Do you have offline or immutable backups, and have you tested restoring them?
questions.fix: Keep offline/immutable backups and test a restore.

questions.q: Is there a named security official responsible for HIPAA security?
questions.fix: Formally designate a security official.

questions.q: Do you have a written incident and breach response plan that covers notification timelines?
questions.fix: Write an incident and breach notification plan and practice it.

soc2.title: SOC 2
soc2.blurb: For SaaS and service companies whose customers ask for a SOC 2 report.

questions.q: Have you decided which Trust Services Criteria and which systems are in scope for your SOC 2?
questions.fix: Define your SOC 2 scope and criteria before buying tools or hiring an auditor.

questions.q: Do you have written, approved security policies that employees acknowledge?
questions.fix: Adopt a right-sized policy set and collect employee acknowledgments.

questions.q: Are access reviews performed at least quarterly, with joiner/mover/leaver steps documented?
questions.fix: Start quarterly access reviews and a documented onboarding/offboarding checklist.

questions.q: Do code and infrastructure changes go through review and approval before production?
questions.fix: Require peer review and approval for production changes.

questions.q: Do you assess the security of critical vendors and keep evidence of it?
questions.fix: Build a simple vendor risk review for critical suppliers.

questions.q: Are logging, monitoring, and alerting in place for production systems?
questions.fix: Turn on centralized logging and alerting for production.

questions.q: Have you run a risk assessment and documented how each risk is treated?
questions.fix: Run and document an annual risk assessment.

questions.q: Are you collecting evidence continuously (screenshots, tickets, reports) rather than right before the audit?
questions.fix: Set up continuous evidence collection so the audit window is not a scramble.

insurance.title: Cyber insurance readiness
insurance.blurb: For any business applying for or renewing cyber insurance.

questions.q: Is multi-factor authentication enforced on email, remote access, and all admin accounts?
questions.fix: Enforce MFA everywhere insurers check: email, remote access, and admin accounts.

questions.q: Do you have endpoint detection and response (EDR) on all laptops and servers?
questions.fix: Deploy EDR on every endpoint and server.

questions.q: Are backups offline or immutable, and have you tested a full restore in the last year?
questions.fix: Make backups offline/immutable and test a restore.

questions.q: Are security patches applied to critical systems within 30 days?
questions.fix: Set a patching cadence with a 30-day target for critical systems.

questions.q: Do you filter email for phishing and train staff to report suspicious messages?
questions.fix: Add email filtering and phishing-reporting training.

questions.q: Are privileged/admin accounts separate from everyday user accounts?
questions.fix: Separate admin accounts from daily-use accounts.

questions.q: Do you have an incident response plan with your insurer's breach hotline listed?
questions.fix: Write an incident response plan that starts with your insurer's hotline.

questions.q: Do you require call-back verification before changing payment or banking details?
questions.fix: Require out-of-band verification for any payment or bank-detail change.

aigov.title: AI governance
aigov.blurb: For companies adopting AI tools or agents (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act).
aigov.framework: AI Governance (NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 / EU AI Act)

questions.q: Do you have an inventory of the AI tools, models, and agents your company uses, including free tools employees use on their own?
questions.fix: Build an AI inventory that includes shadow AI tools.

questions.q: Do you have an AI acceptable-use policy that says what data may and may not be put into AI tools?
questions.fix: Publish a short AI acceptable-use policy with clear data rules.

questions.q: Is someone accountable for AI risk decisions (a named owner or committee)?
questions.fix: Name an accountable AI risk owner.

questions.q: Do you review AI vendors for data use, retention, and model-training terms before approving them?
questions.fix: Add AI-specific questions to vendor reviews (training on your data, retention, location).

questions.q: Do you know whether any of your AI uses would count as high-risk under the EU AI Act or similar laws?
questions.fix: Classify each AI use case by regulatory risk level.

questions.q: Are AI agents limited to the least access they need, with human approval for risky actions?
questions.fix: Apply least privilege and human approval steps to AI agents.

questions.q: Do you test AI features for prompt injection, data leakage, and harmful output before release?
questions.fix: Add AI security testing (prompt injection, leakage) to your release process.

questions.q: Do you monitor AI use and outputs after deployment and have a way to report AI incidents?
questions.fix: Monitor AI use in production and define an AI incident path.
